checks.explanation: The Palmer Luckey All-In Summit session was released as a podcast episode shortly after this recording, consistent with the prediction.

The May 2022 CPI report released that Friday showed inflation still very elevated (around 8.6% year-over-year, actually higher than expected), and markets sold off sharply rather than rallying, contradicting this prediction's conditional outcome.
The US did record two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth in Q1 and Q2 2022, technically meeting the definition of recession, consistent with this prediction.

The Fed raised rates by 75 basis points (not 50) at both the June and July 2022 FOMC meetings after the hot May CPI report, exceeding the predicted 50bp pace, and did not pause in the back half of 2022, continuing to hike through year-end.

Equity markets did continue falling into October 2022 amid earnings concerns, roughly consistent with the predicted 2-3 quarter window for finding a low, though the precise causal mechanism of broad earnings-forecast revisions driving the exact bottom is difficult to isolate.

Structured venture deals with liquidation preferences and other downside-protection terms did become notably more common in late 2022 as startups sought to avoid formal down rounds amid worsening financing conditions.
The tech talent market did cool substantially by late 2022, with widespread layoffs across the industry reducing competition for candidates and easing upward pressure on compensation.

By fall 2022 there were some signs inflation was moderating from its June peak, but it remained elevated and volatile through year-end, and equity valuations did not clearly return to a stable 5-year-average multiple regime during that period given continued Fed tightening and market declines into October.

The US avoided runaway inflation and public markets did stabilize by late 2022/early 2023, but venture markets took considerably longer than 6-12 months to reach a genuinely investable, market-clearing environment, with the funding slump persisting well into 2023 and 2024.
The layoffs.fyi tracker did surpass 3,000 companies with reported layoffs as the tech downturn extended through 2022 and 2023.
Friedberg returned to the podcast in subsequent episodes and the Palmer Luckey episode was indeed released as planned around that time.
